With a new sponsor, United Bank, the number of stream was cut from four to two, an Inland stream and a Coastal stream of 20 teams each.{{Cite web |title=Premier Soccer League - www.psl.co.za - official website |url=https://www.psl.co.za/content/16306 |access-date=2023-09-06 |website=www.psl.co.za}}{{Cite web |title=South Africa 1998/99 |url=https://www.rsssf.org/tablesz/zaf98.html |access-date=2023-09-06 |website=www.rsssf.org}} The Coastal stream was won by [[Dynamos F.C. (South Africa)|Dynamos]] and the Inland stream by [[Seven Stars F.C.|Seven Stars]], with both earning promotion to the [[1998–99 Premier Soccer League]].{{Cite web |title=PSL Clubs since 1994 |url=https://www.pressreader.com/south-africa/kick-off/20190201/281599536706176 |access-date=2023-09-03 |via=PressReader}} The number of teams was again reduced at the end of the season, with the Coastal stream being reduced to 14 teams, and the Inland stream to 16 teams, in the [[1998–99 National First Division|1998–99 season]]. ==Coastal stream== ===League table=== {{#invoke:Sports table|main|style=WDL |res_col_header=PQR |update=complete |source= |team1=WIN |name_WIN = [[Seven Stars F.C.|Seven Stars]] |team2=VAS |name_VAS = [[Michau Warriors F.C.|Michau Warriors]] |team3=LOU |name_LOU = Wynberg St Johns |team4=MAR |name_MAR = [[Saxon Rovers F.C.|Saxon Rovers]] |team5=WIT |name_WIT = [[Lamontville Golden Arrows F.C.|Golden Arrows]] |team6=AVE |name_AVE = [[Avendale Athletico]] |team7=BEN |name_BEN = Park United |team8=DUR |name_DUR = Royal Tigers |team9=PJ |name_PJ = Milano |team10=CIT |name_CIT = Trinitarians |team11=TIG |name_TIG = Bush Bucks |team12=PRE |name_PRE = [[Vasco da Gama (South Africa)|Vasco da Gama]] |team13=FC |name_FC = FN Rangers |team14=ZUL |name_ZUL = [[Maritzburg United F.C.|Maritzburg United]] |team15=BLA |name_BLA = [[Blackburn Rovers F.C.
